When r = 1, M(1, L, c2) is isomorphic to Sc2., the Hilbert scheme of O-dimensional closed subschemes in S of length c2. Fogarty showed that Sir (n € Z>o) is a smooth projective variety of dimension 2n |Fog68 and computed its Picard group [Fog73]. The Betti numbers of S(r) were completely determined by Göttsche [GÖ0]. When r ≥ 2, M(r, L, c2) can be reducible or non-reduced. But starting from Donaldson's generic smoothness result Don90|, the study of M(r, L, c2) has revealed that M(r, L, c2) has better geometric properties as we fix r ≥ 2, L, and let c2 increase. For example, when c2 is large enough, Gieseker-Li [GL94] [GL96] and O'Grady [O'G96] showed that M(r, L, c2) is irreducible, normal, and generically smooth of expected dimension. Some asymptotic phenomena also occur in the Picard group and Betti numbers of M(r, L, c2) (r ≥ 2) [Qin92||L196||L197||CW22|. This raises a natural question: Question 1.1. Are there asymptotic phenomena similar to those above in the geometry of M(r, L, c2) when r = 0? Sheaves on S of rank zero are supported on points or curves. In this paper, we focus on those pure sheaves supported on curves, which are called one-dimensional sheaves. In contrast to the positive rank case, there are few general results for the moduli space of one-dimensional sheaves. An essential difficulty is that the supports of one-dimensional sheaves can be singular, even non-reduced. To distinguish this case, we use the following notation. Given a nonzero effective divisor & on S and an integer X, denote by MB, the moduli space parametrizing polystable one-dimensional sheaves F on S, with determinant det (F) = Os(ß) and Euler characteristic (F) = X. We will make the following assumption on ß, unless otherwise stated. Assumption 1.2. The following conditions hold: (1) B is base-point-free. (2) A general curve in B is smooth and connected. A conjecture [SZ24, Conjecture 1.3] was proposed on the stabilization of (intersection cohomology) Betti numbers of MB, when x is fixed and B is sufficiently positive, as an analogue of [CW22, Conjecture 1.1]. When S is a del Pezzo surface, this conjecture was resolved in [PSSZ24] by proving an asymptotic formula of the refined BPS invariants which also refine the Betti numbers. The primary motivation of this paper is to explore the stabilization of the Picard number p(Max) of M3,x when B is sufficiently positive. Here, the Picard number p(X) of a proper scheme X is defined as the dimension of the Q-vector space Numo (X) of the numerically equivalence classes of line bundles on X with rational coefficients, in the sense of [Kle66]. We say a divisor ß on S satisfies (P) if (1) B satisfies Assumption 1.2. (2) The arithmetic genus Pa (B) > O.
